content.user_title: Build Persistent Azure AI Agents in .NET
content.value_statement: Developers need concise guidance for the Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK. This skill explains core .NET workflows for agents, tools, streaming, files, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation and required Azure environment variables.
Explains client setup with PersistentAgentsClient and DefaultAzureCredential.
Covers agents, threads, messages, runs, polling, and streaming responses.
Documents tool patterns for function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search.
Lists cleanup, error handling, key SDK types, and related reference links.
limitations: Requires an Azure AI project, deployed model, and valid Azure credentials.
Does not replace testing against the user's Azure tenant and SDK version.
Examples are guidance snippets, not a complete production application.
Tool behavior depends on configured Azure resources and service permissions.

use_cases.title: Create a first agent workflow
use_cases.description: Use the guide to connect the client, create an agent, start a thread, send a message, and read responses.

use_cases.title: Add external knowledge tools
use_cases.description: Review file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search patterns before adding retrieval to an assistant.

use_cases.title: Review SDK concepts quickly
use_cases.description: Use the type tables and workflow sections to understand agents, runs, messages, tool resources, and cleanup tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new .NET project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the minimum steps for creating an Azure AI persistent agent in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Plan streaming responses
prompt_templates.scenario: Add real-time output to an existing agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how polling differs from streaming for Azure AI Agents Persistent in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a tool integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Select retrieval or action tools for an assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search for my .NET agent.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for lifecycle and error handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose a production-ready Azure AI Agents Persistent .NET flow with cleanup, errors, and run status handling.

output_examples.input: Explain the basic Azure AI Agents Persistent workflow for .NET.
output_examples.output: A concise sequence covering package setup, client authentication, agent creation, thread creation, message submission, run execution, response retrieval, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Which tool should I use for document search in my agent?
output_examples.output: A comparison of file search with vector stores and Azure AI Search, including when each option fits document retrieval needs.

output_examples.input: What should I check before production use?
output_examples.output: A checklist covering credentials, service permissions, run status handling, tool validation, resource cleanup, error handling, and SDK version testing.

best_practices: Store endpoint, deployment, and connection identifiers in environment-specific configuration.
Handle every run status, including required action, failure, cancellation, and completion.
Delete temporary agents, threads, files, and vector stores when they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Do not assume sample snippets are production-ready without tenant-specific validation.
Do not ignore failed, cancelled, or required-action run states in polling loops.
Do not leave uploaded files or vector stores unmanaged after testing.

faq.question: What SDK does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.AI.Agents.Persistent for .NET and related Azure Identity setup.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains SDK usage and expects the user to provide Azure resources and credentials.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include streaming guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows the streaming update flow and contrasts it with polling.

faq.question: Which tools are covered?
faq.answer: It covers code interpreter, file search, function calling, Bing grounding, Azure AI Search, OpenAPI, Azure Functions, MCP, SharePoint, and Fabric.

faq.question: What should I validate before deployment?
faq.answer: Validate SDK version, Azure permissions, model deployment, connection IDs, tool behavior, error handling, and cleanup rules.
